_comment: Every machine you can remote into. The gateway runs on the always-on box
and dials these over the tailnet, so a laptop being asleep or booted into
the other OS is a normal state the UI reports, not a failure.
monitors:
primary-switch  gnome-remote-desktop streams ONE monitor (whichever is
primary). Switching rebuilds the session, so this needs
the host agent — see agent/README.md.
multimon        the RDP server sends every screen in one stream; the
client crops locally, so switching is instant. Windows
can do this.
single          one screen, no switching.
host is whatever your tailnet calls the machine. A MagicDNS name beats a
100.x address, which can change when a node is re-authed.
password and agent.token are blank ON PURPOSE. Fill them in your own
devices.json — that file is gitignored; this one is committed.
ssh is optional and independent of how the pixels arrive: a machine can
have a desktop AND a terminal, or nothing but a terminal (transport
"ssh", as the last device here). Auth is keyFile, or password, or
neither — with neither, the gateway's own ssh-agent is used.
fingerprint is the host key to expect; leave it out and the first
connection logs the one it saw, so there is something to paste in.
name: LOQ · Linux

_comment: A headless box: no screen to take over, but a shell to work in. It
shows up in the Shell view only, and its presence is sshd answering.
port defaults to 22, host and username default to the device's.
name: Home server
